verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter was a $327.6 million NASA probe.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The Mars Surveyor '98 program spacecraft development cost 193.1 million dollars. Launch costs are estimated at 91.7 million dollars and mission operations at 42.8 million dollars.' (totals 327.6M); R4: '$327.6 million probe'
verifications.reasoning: R1 costs sum exactly to 327.6M for the MCO program; R4 directly attributes to the probe.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter was launched on December 11, 1998.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Mars Climate Orbiter was launched... on 11 December 1998'; R2: 'Launch Dec. 11, 1998'; R3: 'launched on December 11, 1998'; R4: 'launched on December 11, 1998'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the exact date.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter was to study the Martian climate.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The two missions were to study the Martian weather, climate, and water and carbon dioxide budget'; 'primary science objectives to: monitor the daily weather and atmospheric conditions'
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly lists studying Martian climate as a key objective.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter failed on September 23, 1999.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'executed... on 23 September 1999'; R2: 'End of Mission Sept. 23, 1999'; R3: 'September 23, 1999'; R4: 'September 23, 1999'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm failure/loss on this exact date.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter entered the atmosphere too low and burned up.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'entering the Martian atmosphere at an altitude of 57 km... destroyed by atmospheric stresses and friction'; R2: 'the spacecraft burned up in Mars' atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: References directly describe low entry and destruction/burn-up.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter failure was caused by a navigation error.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'destroyed when a navigation error caused it to miss its target altitude'; R2: 'unsuccessful due to a navigation error'
verifications.reasoning: Both directly attribute failure to navigation error.

verifications.claim: The navigation error was a failure to convert English units to metric between teams.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'navigation error resulted from some spacecraft commands being sent in English units instead of being converted to metric'; R2: 'failure to translate English units to metric'; R3: 'failure to use metric units... thruster performance data in English units'; R4: 'Lockheed Martin calculated... imperial units... JPL expected metric'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm units mismatch (English/Imperial to metric) as cause.

verifications.claim: Lockheed Martin-engineered software calculated thruster force in Imperial units (pound-seconds).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Lockheed Martin calculated thruster force in imperial units (pound-seconds)'
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states Lockheed software used Imperial pound-seconds for thruster force.

verifications.claim: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) expected metric (Newton-seconds).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) expected metric (Newton-seconds)'
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly attributes metric Newton-seconds expectation to JPL.

verifications.claim: The units discrepancy caused an in-flight trajectory error.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'navigation error resulted from... English units... caused the spacecraft to miss its intended... altitude'; R3: 'data in English... resulted in small errors... in the trajectory'; R4: 'miscalculated trajectory'
verifications.reasoning: References link units discrepancy directly to trajectory error.

verifications.claim: Communication was lost on September 23, 1999, at 09:04:52 UTC.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The spacecraft's carrier signal was last seen at approximately 09:04:52 UTC on Thursday, September 23, 1999'
verifications.reasoning: R3 provides the exact time and date of last contact.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter mission goal was to act as a weather orbiter.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'orbit Mars as the first interplanetary weather satellite'; R1: 'monitor the daily weather and atmospheric conditions'
verifications.reasoning: R3 explicitly calls it a weather satellite; R1 details weather monitoring goals.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter mission goal was to act as a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'serve as a data relay satellite for the Mars Polar Lander'; R2: 'serve as a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander'; R3: 'provide a communications relay for the Mars Polar Lander'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references confirm relay role for Mars Polar Lander.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter was expected to fly at 150 km above Mars.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'miss its intended 140 - 150 km altitude above Mars during orbit insertion'
verifications.reasoning: R1 specifies target altitude as 140-150 km, including 150 km.

verifications.claim: The Mars Climate Orbiter dropped to 57 km.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'entering the Martian atmosphere at an altitude of 57 km'; R4: 'dropped to 57 km'
verifications.reasoning: Both confirm exact altitude of 57 km.

verifications.claim: The drop resulted in the orbiter's destruction.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The spacecraft would have been destroyed by atmospheric stresses and friction at this low altitude'; R3: 'MCO either was destroyed in the atmosphere'
verifications.reasoning: References directly link low altitude drop to destruction.

verifications.claim: The investigation highlighted a lack of end-to-end testing.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference mentions 'end-to-end testing'; closest is general verification/validation issues in R3.

verifications.claim: The investigation highlighted poor communication within the project.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Contributing Causes: ... Inadequate communications between project elements'
verifications.reasoning: R3 explicitly lists inadequate communications as a contributing cause.
